story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price BSE to move about ±8.1%, roughly 3,642 to 4,288. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 57% of the time.

Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap +0.4 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for BSE: against the past year the gap is on the high side, so less fear is priced than usual.
Options on BSE are priced for moves of about 2.19% a day. That is on the low side for BSE compared with the past year.

For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 4,000 (+1.4% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 3,800 (-3.7%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.

iv.simple: Options on BSE are priced for moves of about 2.19% a day. That is on the low side for BSE compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 34.7%: 20th percentile of 1 year, 10th of all days since 2024-11-29.

vrp.simple: Options are priced close to how much BSE has really been moving (about 34.7% a year).
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -0.0 vol points, 43rd percentile of the past year. Since 2024-11-29, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 46% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

term.simple: Longer-dated options on BSE cost more than near ones: the normal, calm shape.

skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal +0.37 vol pts (front month), 83rd percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: BSE has actually been moving about 2.19% a day this past month: normal for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 34.8% (42nd percentile of the past year), RV5 42.4%, RV63 36.3%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 77th percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 4,000 (+1.4% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 3,800 (-3.7%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.68; all-expiry OI PCR at the 59th percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +515,800, puts -58,800 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: BSE futures trade 17.7 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 5.1% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +17.7, annualised carry 5.1% (41st percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 5.7%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Long unwinding, Long unwinding, Short covering, Long build-up, Short build-up. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.simple: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price BSE to move about ±8.1%, roughly 3,642 to 4,288. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 57% of the time.
move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 8.15% (forward 3,965.4). Scored on 491 days since 2024-11-29 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.

notes.text: BSE has used 15% of its market-wide position limit (the ban starts at 95%).
